 Ateneo’s Tuano handed one-game suspension, out for UE showdown 
 November 17, 2026 | 7:05 pm 
 ATENEO DE MANILA UNIVERSITY 
vs University of Santo Tomas — UAAP 
 ATENEO de Manila University (ADMU) took another hit on its way to elimination as forward Shawn Tuano was handed a one-game suspension in the tail end of the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball.
 Mr. Tuano accumulated two unsportsmanlike fouls for the season for a one-game ban which he will serve on Nov. 25 against also-ran University of the East (UE) at the Mall of Asia Arena.
 He reached the limit after an “unnecessary and uncalled for push” on University of Santo Tomas’ Collins Akowe during a deadball situation last weekend after Jared Bahay’s previous foul. Mr. Akowe fell on to the floor after the shove from Mr. Tuano as the UAAP deemed no provocation to warrant the said act. 
 The incident happened in the last 21 seconds of the fourth quarter as Santo Tomas scored a huge 89-84 win to boost its Final Four hopes at 7-6 and eliminate Ateneo at 5-8.
 Mr. Tuano’s first infraction came in the first round after accidentally hitting the face of Far Eastern University (FEU) center Mo Konateh during a shot challenge in the 4:06 mark of the third period.
 His suspension will run smack right on head coach Louie Alas’ return from a two-game suspension after committing additional unsportsmanlike conducts from his first suspension in the first round.
 Mr. Alas’ absence in the past two games closed the door on the ADMU Blue Eagles’ Final Four chances, absorbing a 62-55 loss against Adamson University then versus Santo Tomas to get the boot entering its non-bearing final match against University of the East.
 Aside from Ateneo and UE (1-11), Adamson is also out of the Final Four at 5-8. Only reigning champion De La Salle University (7-5), Far Eastern University (7-5) and Santo Tomas (7-6) are in the running for the final two spots as National University (NU) (9-3) and University of the Philippines (UP) (9-3) are already in. 
 The UAAP is in the middle of a week-long break for the 49 th ASEAN Summit, plunging back into action on Saturday at the Smart Araneta Coliseum featuring crucial battles between FEU and NU as well as rivals UP and La Salle. — John Bryan Ulanday
